claim: Review-level synthesis: this 2019 tutorial survey provides decision-grade evidence for field-map terminology, conceptual taxonomy, architecture lineage and gap synthesis. It organizes impedance control around force–motion ports, impedance/admittance causality, isolated versus coupled stability, hardware versus software compliance, and position-, torque- and model-based realizations, while classifying force-tracking, hybrid, robust, adaptive, variable and learning controllers. It is not primary causal or quantitative evidence and does not establish method superiority or deployment safety.
claim_locator: Definitions; stability and implementation architectures; controller taxonomy and Table I; massage simulation; conclusion.
epistemic_status: review-level synthesis suitable only for field taxonomy, terminology, architecture lineage and gap identification
problem_and_setting: Organizing robot dynamic interaction across free motion, transition and contact under uncertain environments, finite bandwidth, modeling error, noise and sampling limits.
method_or_mechanism: Uses Z=F/Xdot and port causality; separates isolated and coupled stability; contrasts hardware/software compliance and position-, torque- and model-based implementations; groups later robust, adaptive, variable and learning methods. Passivity is a sufficient route for passive-environment coupling chiefly in linear one-port positive-real settings.
content_summary: The survey synthesizes concepts through 2018. Unified free/contact behavior depends on suitable impedance, bandwidth, sensing, modeling and coupled-stability analysis. Table I is qualitative. A one-dimensional MATLAB massage example is illustrative, not human or clinical evidence. Application breadth is heterogeneous. Future needs include systematic parameter design, robust/adaptive hardware, learning integration and broader trials.
synthesis_role: Historical and conceptual scaffold for the Active Field Map; not a basis for ranking methods or deployment readiness.
development_link: Links classical port/passivity theory to robust, adaptive, variable and learning impedance, marking unresolved design and validation gaps.

evidence.finding: Frames interaction through Z=F/Xdot and distinguishes impedance from admittance causality.
Separates isolated from coupled stability and presents passivity as sufficient under passive linear one-port assumptions.
Organizes hardware/software compliance and position-, torque- and model-based realization.
Classifies controller families without meta-analytic comparison.
One-dimensional assumed human-back changes provide no human-subject or clinical evidence.
Position filtering requires sampling well above signal bandwidth; model, environment, noise and sampling errors can undermine behavior.
Identifies parameter design, hardware robustness, learning integration and broader trials as gaps.

boundary_conditions: Passivity treatment is chiefly passive-environment linear one-port.
Table I cannot rank methods quantitatively.
Massage is not a human experiment.
No reproducible systematic-review protocol or quality appraisal exists.
Decision-grade applies only to field-map concepts and lineage.
assumptions: The interaction port meaningfully represents the task.
Models, sensing, bandwidth and sampling are adequate.
Cited literature is representative despite narrative selection.

reported: Inappropriate models, unknown environments, error, noise and low sampling can undermine control.
Systematic parameter design and validation remain unresolved.
inferred: Completeness and selection bias cannot be assessed.
Heterogeneous applications cannot support causal superiority.
Conditional passivity is not universal safety.

verification_status: verified against Controller-supplied admitted full text
